title: Benchmarking Trustworthiness of SLMs: Pre-trained vs. Compressed
abstract: arXiv:2608.11981v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Small Language Models (SLMs) have emerged as a more efficient alternative to traditional Large Language Models (LLMs), offering promising potential in resource-constrained scenarios. Existing approaches to building SLMs typically follow two paths: training compact models from scratch, or compressing larger pre-trained models using methods such as pruning, quantization, or distillation. As language models become increasingly integrated into real-world applications, ensuring their trustworthiness has become a critical concern. However, how to build trustworthy SLMs remains an underexplored question. In this work, we present a comprehensive evaluation of SLM trustworthiness across multiple dimensions, including fairness, robustness, privacy, and ethics. translated_title: 小型语言模型可信度基准测试：预训练模型与压缩模型对比
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.11981v1 公告类型：新 摘要：小型语言模型（SLMs）已成为传统大型语言模型（LLMs）更高效的替代方案，在资源受限场景中展现出巨大潜力。构建SLMs的现有方法通常遵循两条路径：从头训练紧凑模型，或使用剪枝、量化或蒸馏等方法压缩大型预训练模型。随着语言模型日益融入实际应用，确保其可信度已成为关键问题。然而，如何构建可信的SLMs仍是一个未被充分探索的问题。在本工作中，我们对SLM的可信度进行了多维度综合评估，包括公平性、鲁棒性、隐私和伦理。我们首先考察了剪枝和量化的影响，发现与剪枝相比，量化在保持可信度方面显著更有效。更重要的是，我们发...
tldr: 本研究首次系统评估小型语言模型的可信度，发现量化压缩比剪枝更能有效保持模型的公平性、鲁棒性、隐私和伦理性能，为构建可信SLM提供了关键见解。
en_tdlr: This study provides the first systematic evaluation of SLM trustworthiness, revealing that quantization preserves fairness, robustness, privacy, and ethics better than pruning, offering key insights for building trustworthy SLMs.
